service_boundary: Represents Cloudflare's gateway product, not the upstream providers it fronts or Cloudflare's own model hosting.
regional_controls: Requests traverse the operator's global network; no gateway-level control over processing geography is documented.
retention_controls: Persistent log volumes differ by plan, and log forwarding is available on paid plans. Customer-supplied provider credentials can be stored so that the operator never holds the billing relationship.
routing: Caching, rate limiting, and request retry are configurable per gateway, and credential precedence runs from the request, to stored keys, to the operator's own billing.
customization: The gateway fronts existing provider APIs in their native formats; customer fine-tuning is not part of the product.
strengths: Core caching, rate limiting, and analytics are available without charge on a free account and require no infrastructure.
Customer-supplied provider credentials remove the operator from the billing path entirely.
Data-loss prevention scanning is available on all plans rather than reserved for paid tiers.
tradeoffs: Providers connect through their own native request formats, and a single compatible endpoint across providers could not be confirmed from the documentation.
Persistent log retention is capped far lower on the free tier, and forwarding logs elsewhere requires a paid plan.
Credits bought through the operator's unified billing carry a stated percentage fee, avoidable only by supplying provider keys.

response_integrity.note: No signature, attestation, or equivalent mechanism for verifying that a response arrived unaltered from the upstream model appears in the AI Gateway overview, providers, caching, or bring-your-own-keys documentation.
response_integrity.scope: Cloudflare AI Gateway documentation, for Cloudflare AI Gateway

upstream_disclosure.note: The providers page ("Connect to AI providers using their native API formats through AI Gateway.") lists the twenty-four upstream providers a gateway can be configured for, from Workers AI and Amazon Bedrock through OpenAI, OpenRouter, and xAI; request content reaches whichever named provider a route targets.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Cloudflare AI Gateway providers page, for Cloudflare AI Gateway

credential_handling.note: The bring-your-own-keys page states keys are stored with Secrets Store, whose page states: "The secrets are securely encrypted and stored across all Cloudflare data centers." The encryption statement sits on the Secrets Store page rather than the AI Gateway page.
credential_handling.scope: Cloudflare Secrets Store documentation, read for AI Gateway bring-your-own-keys

cache_isolation.note: The caching page documents the cache key: "By default, AI Gateway constructs the cache key by concatenating the following and hashing the result with SHA-256: Provider (for example, openai, anthropic), Endpoint (the API path), Model (for example, gpt-4o), Provider authentication header (for example, the Authorization bearer token), Full request body." Entries are therefore keyed to the credential in use; the page does not address scope when Cloudflare-supplied rather than customer credentials are used.
cache_isolation.scope: Cloudflare AI Gateway caching page, for Cloudflare AI Gateway

vulnerability_disclosure.note: A platform-wide security.txt names a disclosure programme ("Contact: https://hackerone.com/cloudflare") and a policy page. AI Gateway is operated on the same domain under the same programme.
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: Cloudflare security.txt, for Cloudflare AI Gateway

independent_audit.note: The SOC 2 page's in-scope product list names the service: "Browser Rendering, Cloudflare Images, Cloudflare for SaaS, D1, Durable Objects, Hyperdrive, Pages, R2, Stream, Vectorize, Workers, Workers AI, Cloudflare Workers KV, AI Gateway, Cloudflare Queues". Scope is revised on an annual audit cycle.
independent_audit.scope: Cloudflare SOC 2 compliance page, for Cloudflare AI Gateway
